title: Only God remains
takeaway: Seasons change and people leave, but God remains forever.
scene: Two short four-line verses on page 87, with no titles. The first mourns the loss of good friends. The second reflects on how everything changes except God.

original: چنگے ساتھی ٹر جان تے ہوئے جگ ہنیر
کالی رات دا پہرا رہندا ہوئے نہ کدی سویر
transliteration: Change saathi tur jaan te hoe jag haner
Kaali raat da pehra rehnda, hoe na kadi saver
translation: When good companions leave, the world goes dark;
the dark night stands guard, and morning never comes.
couplets.story: When good friends die, it feels like the whole world has gone dark, like a night that never ends.

original: ناز گیا کر سنجھا احمدؔ گلشن شعر ادب دا
سجن وری دے پھل کھلارن آوناں نئیں اوس فیر
transliteration: Naaz gaya kar sunjha Ahmad gulshan shair adab da
Sukhan-vari de phull khilaaran aavnaan nahin os pher
translation: Ahmad, Naz has gone and left the garden of poetry and literature empty;
he won't come back to scatter the flowers of poetry again.
couplets.story: A friend named Naz has died, and the 'garden' of poetry feels empty without him. He won't be coming back to share his beautiful poems.

original: رتاں بدل دیاں رہندیاں ہر ویلے اعلیٰ قدرت دا ہے نظام ہردم
سورج چن تارے نویں زندگی دا دیندے رہندے نیں نواں پیغام ہردم
transliteration: Rutaan badaldiyaan rehndiyaan har vele, aala qudrat da hai nizaam har dam
Sooraj chann taare naveen zindagi da dende rehnde nain navaan paighaam har dam
translation: The seasons keep changing all the time: this is nature's perfect system.
The sun, the moon and the stars keep giving a new message of new life, every moment.
couplets.story: Seasons are always changing. That's how God set up the world. The sun, moon and stars keep bringing new days and new life.

original: بناں رب دی ذات نہ کجھ رہنا کسے چیز نوں نئیں دوام ہردم
باریں ورہیں رب روڑی دی وی سن لیندا اسدے رہندے آں احمدؔ اے عام ہردم
transliteration: Binaan Rab di zaat na kujh rehna, kise cheez nu nahin dawaam har dam
Baaraan varheen Rab roorhi di vi sun lainda, asi de rehnde aan Ahmad, ae aam har dam
translation: Except for God Himself, nothing will remain; nothing lasts forever.
Every twelve years God listens even to the rubbish heap, as people often say, Ahmad.
couplets.story: Nothing in the world lasts forever except God. Then a hopeful old Punjabi saying: 'After twelve years, even the rubbish heap's luck turns.' Even the lowest, most forgotten things get their turn when God answers.

deeper: 'Except for God Himself, nothing will remain' echoes the Qur'an: 'Everything on it will perish, and the Face of your Lord will remain' (55:26–27). The changing seasons, sun and stars are signs (ayat) of God's order. The old saying about the rubbish heap is a homely way of saying no one is beyond God's notice.
why: It moves from grief to a calm, big-picture view: everything changes, but God doesn't, and everyone gets their turn eventually.
prompt: When something ends or changes, what helps you hold on to hope?
notes: Two untitled verses on page 87, stored together. 'Naz' may be the same person mourned on page 88 (Gulzar-e-Naz).
Last line: 'Baaraan varheen roorhi di vi sun lainda' is a Punjabi proverb, roughly 'every dog has its day'.
